bucket_definitions.docs_bucket: All files under Docs/ plus every tracked *.md/*.markdown anywhere (explains Docs > Markdown)
bucket_definitions.source: Text files outside test trees, Docs/, *.md, Examples/, Scripts/, and noise prefixes
bucket_definitions.tests: Text files under Tests/, BlazeDBTests/, BlazeDBIntegrationTests/, BlazeDBCLITests/, BlazeDBVisualizerTests/, BlazeDBExtraTests/, BlazeDBTests_SPM/
bucket_definitions.text_files: Tracked paths that exist on disk and are not binary (extension denylist + NUL check)

ci_lane_coverage.android: PR gate: cross-compile + KMM emulator smoke — no SPM XCTest tier execution
ci_lane_coverage.linux: PR Tier0+CLITests; nightly Tier1+Tier2; weekly Extended+Heavy(+Perf)
ci_lane_coverage.macos: PR Tier0+Tier1; nightly Tier2; weekly Tier3/Heavy/Perf/Destructive

docs.why_docs_bucket_exceeds_markdown: Docs bucket = all files under Docs/ (any extension) plus every tracked *.md anywhere. Markdown count is *.md only. Non-Markdown under Docs/ (txt, json, scripts, exports) and double-counting rules explain the gap.

methodology_limitations: Named XCTest methods ≠ executed cases (parameterization, skips, filters).
swift test list may undercount when BLAZEDB_TEST_SCOPE=tier0 or .build is cold/stale.
Documentation inventory classifications are used when the inventory file is present; they are human/agent judgments, not proofs of obsolescence.
Old regression/compatibility tests are never auto-labeled obsolete.
Curated subsystem list is architectural narrative, not a derived metric.
Unreferenced-fixture detection is basename heuristic only.
